'''''Chrysanthemum pacificum''''', commonly called '''gold and silver chrysanthemum''',<ref name=mobot>[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=h600 ''Ajania pacifica''], Missouri Botanical Garden,</ref> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Asteraceae|aster family]]. It is native to [[Japan]], where it is endemic to the island of [[Honshu]]. Its natural habitat is along the Pacific coast, where it often grows on ocean cliffs.<ref name="Ohwi">{{cite book |last=Ohwi |first=Jisaburo |title=Flora of Japan |date=1965 |publisher=Smithsonian Institution |page=891 |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.43786 |lccn=65062683 |oclc=182709297}}</ref><ref name=Okayama>[http://had0.big.ous.ac.jp/plantsdic/angiospermae/dicotyledoneae/sympetalae/compositae/isogiku/isogiku.htm ''Dendranthema pacificum''] (in Japanese), Okayama University Plant Ecology Laboratory</ref>

== Description ==
It is a showy plant, blooming in late fall and producing yellow heads of flowers.<ref name=mobot/> It was introduced into U.S. gardening catalogs in 1989,<ref>{{cite news |last=Lacy |first=Allen |date=1989-01-05 |title=A GARDENER'S WORLD; A Plant Almost Too Good to Be True |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/01/05/garden/a-gardener-s-world-a-plant-almost-too-good-to-be-true.html |work= The New York Times |access-date=2018-01-14 }}</ref> and has been in cultivation in Japan since an early date.<ref name=Okayama/>
